answer: Set `config.set("sync.documents", true)` in a Space Lua block. Yes, where you set it matters: sync configuration must be done in the `CONFIG` page specifically, and it won't be picked up if configured elsewhere.

Memory for: I want PDFs and other attachments to be available offline in the browser client too. What do I set, and does it matter where I set it?
[1] Tag/document.md (document)
  - Every non-page file in your space, such as images, PDFs and attachments, is available via the document tag.
[2] PWA.md (What the PWA gives you)
  - You should let the initial sync finish and test the pages and attachments you need before relying on offline access.
  Limits: Offline startup requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), a working service worker and previously cached application code. Plain LAN HTTP runs online-only. See [[TLS#LAN HTTP (no TLS)]]. Installing the PWA does not change these requirements. / Server-backed [[Search]], shell execution, remote sharing and external network APIs require a connection. Local page navigation, editing and queries over the client Object Index can work with cached data. Let the initial sync finish and test the pages and attachments you need before relying on offline access. Browser storage is not a backup.
[3] Sync.md (Sync)
  - Setting config.set("sync.documents", true) in a Space Lua block in CONFIG syncs documents so they are available offline.
  Configuration: You can tweak what files are synced locally via a few `config.*` configuration options. / > **note** Note / > Sync related configuration **need** to be done in the [[CONFIG]] page specifically. If they are configured elsewhere they will not be picked up. / By default all your pages are synced, but [[Document]] are not. They are fetched on demand. If you would also like to sync documents (so you can access them when offline), you can do so by setting the following in a Space Lua block in [[CONFIG]]: / config.set("sync.documents", true) / In addition, you can fine-tune what files you do _not_ want to sync using [gitignore](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore) pattern syntax assigned to the `sync.ignore` option, which accepts either a single string, or a list of strings. The space folder’s actual `.gitignore` file is not read: / config.set("sync.ignore", { / -- Don't sync PDFs and MP4 files
[4] Document.md (Uploading)
  - Images, video, audio, and PDFs are supported for embedding using the browser's native media elements and range-capable file responses.
[5] Guide/Server Setup.md (Install and create a space)
  - A reset of client storage can discard edits that have not reached the Server, so a Server problem must be distinguished from a browser's offline copy before resetting.
[6] ADR/001 Offline-First PWA.md (Context)
  Context: SilverBullet aims to be **offline-first**: it should keep working with no network and feel instant. While we may reach a point in the state of the world some day where Internet connectivity is always available, we’re not there yet. You should be able to access your notes even when you’re in the middle of a dessert, top of a mountain, or 10km deep in the sea. Exact facts:
- [1] Every non-page file in your space (images, PDFs, attachments, etc.) is available via the `document` tag, they’re indexed purely from filesystem metadata.
- [2] SilverBullet Server’s browser client is a [Progressive Web App](https://web.dev/progressive-web-apps/) (PWA). It can be installed in a standalone window and can read and edit cached content offline. [[Desktop]] is the native application, with files stored in local folders.
